Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
This is probably WAAAAY premature and will make me look pretty silly
after a few weeks, but right now it seems to me that a big strength of SW
is the lack of Power Commons in the boosters. No Govern, no conditioning
[both these still there in precons, which is fine], no KRC, no legal
manipulations, no majesty, misdirection thoroughly knee-capped.

Storage Annex may turn out to be abusable; and The haunting looks like a
dam' fine card. But apart from these, the power commons in SW look like
Undead Strength and Pushing the Limit.

i'm obviously quite pleased by this trend but i wonder if we are about to
see the rise of the Stupid Combat Deck. Just occasionally down here we
get a new or inexperienced player who builds a rush-combat or vote deck
and then just slams around the table spreading random carnage. This can
be amusing or frustrating, but it does now seem to me that there's the
potential for a new player to get hold of the Brujah antitribu deck, beef
it up with a few cards from the boosters, and go to town, resulting in
serious table-unbalancing effects. They won't win, of course, but i think
the assumption that combat is going to be fielded only by really
experienced and skillful players is going to crumble over the next few
months, which has consequences for all of those who play competitively.

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Majesty shouldn't be an issue for a standard rush deck, due to a
variety of strike: combat ends hosing cards - Immortal Grapple is the
fave, but also see Psyche, Thoughts Betrayed, Hidden Lurker, and Fast
Reaction (really Tzimisce only can use this) and the new Telepathic
Tracking (again, really for the fiends or the !Toreador, or some gung
ho Malkavians - don't laugh, I've seen a Malkavian combat deck do quite
well!).

A real favourite for me at the moment is the Obedience technique - get
a high cap vampire with Dominate and jump in the way of a Bums Rush /
Ambush. Most bruise decks don't bother with stealth so you should be
able to block, which means you get to play your Obedience.

The best thing about this is that it "cancels" combat before it happens
rather than "Strike: Combat Ends" combat, so the poor fool with all the
combat cards can't cycle them and ends up with a seven combat card hand
jam. I played this technique to great effect last night, but suffered
from running out of stealth myself and got smashed to pieces! The one
bad thing about Obedience is that it is a reaction card only - not a
combat card.

Failing that, it's down to damage prevention. Best for this is Superior
Mettle or Rolling with the Punches, and for you Gangrel lovers, a Flesh
of Marble / Skin of Night combo keeps you warm and snug.

DH

> card cycling of Shadowfist's Wind on the Mountain. If Majesty isn't a
> good counter to this ripe cheese then please give me more details of
> what is.

Majesty or catatonic fear or Earth Meld with manouevers is a good counter
to this kind of deck alright. So is Obedience or Legacy of Power. So is
fortitude-based damage prevention. There are also cunning tactical things
you can do to send the combat deck at somebody else [not bringing out
vampires for a while and then activating several at once is a good way to
do this]. As for the card cycling, that can quite quickly lead to hand-
jam for a combat deck, which can be very serious because it is usually
the case that for such a deck ONE failed combat is enough to lose you the
game. However, i'm not worried by hearing about combat decks that win -
combat OUGHT to be going toe-to-toe with the other strategies [bleed and
vote] and you SHOULD have to think about the likelihood that you are
going to be rushed when you are building a non-combat deck. What i AM
worried about is the possibility that we could start to see
strategically-incompetent combat decks that just destabilise the whole
table so that you may as well roll a dice to see who wins. Some people i
guess won't even be worried by this - after all, lots of people play
malkavian games and pranks, others play feeble vote decks and some play
massive intercept/Eagles' site deck. There's nothing intrinsically wrong
with these strategies if they are cleverly played and it's a pleasure to
watch a good deck of any of these flavours well-played. Too often,
however, they just mess up the basic predator/prey dynamic which IMO is
the reason that VTES works so very well as a multi-player game.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Andrew wrote:
>>Tom played a deck of this sort last night though it wasn't so stupid
as it won. A combat deck comes across as very broken to me - cycling
cards like crazy and never giving other vampires a chance, no matter
how old they are.>>

<Mouth hangs agap>

Are you on crack, my friend? Combat decks are *so* far from broken that the
light from broken will take a million years to reach them.

Yea. If you stumble across a combat deck and have exactly zero combat defense,
you will be killed. On the down side, however, combat decks are:

-Very difficult to actually win a game with.
-Incredibly card combo intensive, and as such, tend to run out of card.
-Difficult to build effectively.
-Notoriously difficult to get victory points with.
-Easy to defend against, given a bit of planning (fortitude, manuvers,
obediance).

There is a reason that I have been on this newsgroup for literally *years*
trying to convince folks that Rush combat decks can actually win, and are
actually effective--no one believes me.

>>If Majesty isn't a good counter to this ripe cheese then please give me more
details of what is.>>

No, no, you have the dichotomy all wrong. Rush combat exists to be the good
counter to the ripe cheese that is Majesty (or Malk S+B or Minion Tap/5th horse
abuse or any number of other strategies that are way too potent, but for the
existance of a Rush deck).

Again, Rush decks are incredibly difficult to actually win games with--yes, if
you sit down with a deck that has zero combat defense, and your predator is a
Rush deck, you will be ousted very quickly. How is this any different from
sitting down with a deck that has zero bleed defense when your predator is a
bleed deck?

I assure you that Combat decks are incredibly simple to foil. If you are
concerned about one, play the Ventrue, and put in, like, 20% non Majesty combat
defense (Skin of Steel, Obediance), and watch your 20% of deck shut down 100%
of the Rush guy's deck.

Messages.Author: James Hamblin
Messages.Body:
"Andrew S. Davidson" wrote:
>
> On Fri, 10 Nov 2000 10:27:34 GMT, legb...@my-deja.com wrote:

> cards like crazy and never giving other vampires a chance, no matter

> how old they are. It takes the worst of a Doomtown deck which is so
> stacked that you can't lose a shootout and combines it with the evil

> card cycling of Shadowfist's Wind on the Mountain. If Majesty isn't a

> good counter to this ripe cheese then please give me more details of
> what is.

Majesty isn't a good counter, because it's too good of a counter. Let
me explain. If you build a combat deck with no way to deal with Majesty
(or other S:CE), then you're going to be a resounding failure. So most
combat decks include many copies of the anti-S:CE cards: Immortal
Grapple, Psyche!, etc. In turn, a non-combat deck which thinks that
just Majesty will suffice against a dedicated combat deck will die
horribly. So many such decks might include maneuvers to make their
Majestys more effective. So the combat deck puts in some maneuvers.
And so on. So I'm not saying Majesty isn't effective, but there are
many ways to get around it. You can make a deck and have that be your
only combat defense, but you should be aware that you're vulnerable to
being trumped by Immortal Grapple, etc.

BTW, if combat decks were broken, they'd be winning many more
tournaments than they do.

James

Chiropteran Marauder would be rubbish for Shock Troops as it needs
Superior Viscitude to get busy. If you have Master Discipline cards
left after playing your Shock Troops, you are wasting them!

I have been thinking about Shock Troops, and the best things I can
think of for them are:

1) Loads of Auspex for Telepathic Counters / intercept, and play Aura
Reading if in combat

2) Protean for Wolfs Claws / Earth meld and just blocking! (Probably
need KRCG / London Evening Star or Sports Bike / Mr Winthrop)

3) Obfuscate - Get Equiptment / recruit Allies

4) Animalism - Block and do a Trap / Song of Serenity / Carrion Crows /
Aid from Bats combo. With added Cats Guidance!

5) Presence - Use them as an Anti Vote block - loads of Dread Gaze /
Surprise influece with Majesties if blocking.

6)Fortitude - Soak up any damage from blocks, make the predator run out
of Combat cards!

The important thing is that they get -1 stealth on their actions.
Therefore Shadow Twin is too easily intercepted (basic d action), and
since Obtenebration isn't great for combat, you would be throwing away
a troop for no reason - same with Cryptic Missions. But they could work
in connection with a Brainwash / Cario, International Airport deck.

We don't usually have this problem. But then, usually new and
inexperienced players see one of US playing something vicious, and can
learn from observation: "Target Your Prey First, Then Anything
Threatening You." We also try to teach new people up front that
ousting the guy to your left should always be at the focus of
everything you do... and if it doesn't help you oust the guy to your
left, you might want to ask yourself why you're doing it. A Rush
backwards is often a good idea to keep yourself alive long enough to
oust him.. but nothing but defense won't get him dead.

>Tom played a deck of this sort last night though it wasn't so stupid
>as it won. A combat deck comes across as very broken to me - cycling
>cards like crazy and never giving other vampires a chance, no matter
>how old they are. It takes the worst of a Doomtown deck which is so
>stacked that you can't lose a shootout and combines it with the evil
>card cycling of Shadowfist's Wind on the Mountain. If Majesty isn't a
>good counter to this ripe cheese then please give me more details of
>what is.

Flash, THEN Majesty. The Toreador love it, because inferior of both
is sufficient.

Skin of Steel played at superior is a very effective counter as well.
"You punch me for 5, then Blur and hit me for 5 two more times? OK, I
spend one blood and one card and take no damage." Its downside, of
course, is that when nobody is punching you for 15, then you tend to
have a lot of it in your hand.

Obedience, from an older vampire. "SIT! Stay. Good Beast!"

Elysium: Arboretum, or Purchase Pact - if the vampires are appropriate
clans.

Leather Jackets can save your guy for JUST long enough.

The old "Hit back Harder" theory. Include enough nuisance combat in
your own deck so that other combat decks have to slow down going after
you. Simply equipping an Ivory Bow will put a crimp in most
non-Immortal Grapple decks. For anyone with Protean, include some
Wolf Claws, which put a crimp in Immortal Grapple decks big time.
Speaking of IG decks, if you want to slow the non-Celerity versions
down, stick a bunch of Zip Guns in your deck, and block the Bum's
Rush. Free permanent maneuver! If you have sufficient pool gain, .44
Magnums are possibly a better choice, as they let you shoot back for
something significant without taking damage yourself. But those
require equip actions or Disguised Weapon.

Actually, Zip Guns or Fake Out or any other form of maneuver is
usually a fairly effective ploy. Sometimes they'll have the maneuver
card in hand, and catch you. But sometimes not. Of course, long
range decks will just blow your head off anyway... but Majesty and
others work lots better against those.

-- Derek

> intrinsically wrong with these strategies if they are cleverly played
> and it's a pleasure to watch a good deck of any of these flavours
> well-played. Too often, however, they just mess up the basic
> predator/prey dynamic which IMO is the reason that VTES works so very
> well as a multi-player game.

Now this is a puzzle I've often had to work. I love the Tzimisce, and
so I play them regularly. I thoroughly enjoy the reactionary style of
the massive intercept/Eagles' Sight deck. But at the same time, like
you say, this is one of the easiest deck types to ruin the
predator/prey dynamic with. You have to keep blocking your prey, as
that is your primary means of ousting him. But, being reactionary,
you're not fast enough to take him/her out before your grand-prey
builds up.

And then you also have the problem of your predator 'going salmon' when
your deck shuts him down. He turns upstream, possibly forcing his
predator to hold back, forcing *his* predator to hold back, etc., until
now your prey is holding back and you don't have anything to block
anymore.

At my last tournament, this very problem popped up in the final. I'd
put up a serious wall to my predator, and my prey was rarely
taking actions (I think because of my Eagles' Sight). I hadn't played
competitively in quite a while, and I think one of the mistakes I made
in that game was blocking my prey a little too frequently early. If
I'd have saved a bit of those up and let him work his prey a bit, my
grand-prey and grand-predator (winner) wouldn't have been so strong
towards the end. It's something I'll definitely take to the next
tournament with me.

And speaking of next tournament, I believe I'll see a lot more Tzimisce
out there with the additions made to them in SW. IMO, they got the
best help of all the Sabbat clans, and are really going to be a force
to be reckoned with.

p.

Messages.Author: Derek Ray
Messages.Body:
On Fri, 10 Nov 2000 18:18:37 GMT, Tom Kassel <tka...@my-deja.com>
wrote:



It does. But the biggest mistake I see with new players and combat
decks is constantly pointing themselves to the right for anything that
seems remotely like a threat, to the point where they neglect to point
themselves to the left enough.

If Ozmo or Emerson Bridges comes out behind you, they need to go away
immediately, for obvious reasons. Emerson even more so since he is
likely to be packing Fortitude and you may not be able to get him at
your leisure; he may require some effort.

A predator who transfers out Zoe or Agrippina, however, is not
something you need to worry about extensively. Spend your time going
forward, and if Agrippina does anything silly like put a Spying
Mission (read "bullseye") on herself, THEN blow her away. Same with
Zoe; she's only a significant threat to you if your grand-predator is
a big bleeder, and even THEN I might wait around to see if she was a
bleed bouncer or an interceptor.

Pointing yourself left doesn't always imply Rushing all their vamps
into torpor immediately, either, since you want them to hurt their
prey some as well. Kill their first guy. Then you could pretend to
be out of Rush actions and spend a lot of time bleeding for 1. Odds
are they won't block, and while they MIGHT waste the blood Deflecting,
it's a coin flip there. This way, they transfer out more vampires,
and once they get 3 out and have piddled around for a bit, you can
spend one turn and kill all of them in one shot.

Rush decks' best form of bleed is convincing their prey to transfer
out vampires, who are then wholesale bleeds for 4-6. Killing the
first two guys as they come out is likely to provoke them to transfer
all but 1 to a couple, and then stall until you are forced to turn
your attention to your predator more solidly, or until they draw into
their combat defense. (If they have none, they're screwed.)

Messages.Author: Jasper Phillips
Messages.Body:
>"Andrew S. Davidson" wrote:
>>
>> Tom played a deck of this sort last night though it wasn't so stupid
>> as it won. A combat deck comes across as very broken to me - cycling
>> cards like crazy and never giving other vampires a chance, no matter
>> how old they are. It takes the worst of a Doomtown deck which is so
>> stacked that you can't lose a shootout and combines it with the evil
>> card cycling of Shadowfist's Wind on the Mountain. If Majesty isn't a
>> good counter to this ripe cheese then please give me more details of
>> what is.

[replying 2nd hand as my usenet feed lost the original]

Trying to use majesty against a potence rush deck is comparable to trying
to use Fortitude against a Tremere combat deck -- it's just not going to
work as they are built specifically to stop it. This doesn't mean that there
aren't other defenses.

Maneuvers and Fortitude are good general prevention. Majesty is more
effective as a suplement to these kinds of cards. Obedience is great.
The Elysium and Secure Haven are very annoying. Aggravated hand damage
can slow them down, and ranged combat really hoses rush combat. Hell, in
general having anyone who can fight back helps.

IMHO if rush combat were really so cheesy, it would be more effective.

-Jasper

Although Thaumaturgy may not seem like the best choice to choose for the
discipline cards, if you're playing Tremere, you can make heavy use of Tremere
Convocation. This will give all the new shock troops the ability to play
superior thaumaturgy! And they still are a bit expendable -- have the first
shock troop use a superior Burst, sending it's opponent to torpor and burning
itself. With the second shock troop, you diablerize the torpored vamp and the
kicker -- for your new skill card (due to diablerie) you choose the former
shock troop / discipline card!

In addition, though these vampires are clanless, you can still set up a method
of bloatedness. Tribute to the Master along with Media Influence or Blood Feast
can be an effective equivalent to Minion Tap / 5th.
